subject: On-prem cutover — ephemeral NAT rewrite causing TCP fragmentation and SG blocking
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@stratacorp.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-cutover failures — TCP resets + large payload drops

Hi Olga / Marissa,

We completed the private deployment cutover to Redwood Private v2 last night (window 02:00-03:30 PDT). Since the cutover, several backend services are seeing intermittent TCP resets and failed large-file uploads (S3-like storage). The errors look like packets getting truncated or dropped mid-flow — clients show 413 / ECONNRESET.

Attached is a short pcap-ish trace (textified) from one of our app servers and an excerpt of our edge NAT translation table. You can see many flows being SNAT'd to ephemeral ports in the 61000 range and timeouts around the same time as the resets.

We rolled back to the previous routing (briefly) and failures reduced but returned after the reroute. Can you advise urgently? This is impacting our nightly batch jobs.

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
NetOps Lead, StrataCorp
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-cutover failures — TCP resets + large payload drops

Hi team,

Escalating — StrataCorp is seeing TCP resets + large payloads failing after our private cutover. They attached traces showing SNAT ephemeral port usage and packet truncation. I already pinged them for additional pcaps and interface counters, but please review and flag immediate mitigations.

Initial hypotheses:
- MTU mismatch / path MTU discovery failing (DF set, fragments dropped by an intermediate device)
- SNAT ephemeral port port-space exhaustion or port-aliasing causing connection collisions
- Security group/stateful firewall dropping fragments or reassembled packets due to TCP offload mismatch

Immediate ask: confirm whether the NAT rewrite we applied (ephemeral SNAT mapping) also changed the MSS/PMTU clamp behavior on the edge appliance. Also check if we enabled TSO/GSO passthrough that would expose large segments to the path.

I'll coordinate customer comms.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Network Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-cutover failures — TCP resets + large payload drops

Thanks for the ping. Quick notes from runtime:
- The v2 edge NAT module introduced a different source-port allocation algorithm to reduce churn; it should not exhaust ports but can reuse ephemeral ports faster under high churn.
- We did not change the MTU or MSS clamp config by intent — however the kernel-level offload flags were toggled to improve throughput during the rollout. That might cause TX segment sizes to exceed PMTU until the clamp is applied.

Immediate mitigation options (choose 1 for urgent rollout):
1) Apply MSS clamp on the edge egress interface for StrataCorp prefix to 1400 (safe for most paths) — config change, low risk, quick rollback.
2) Temporarily widen SNAT port pool to avoid collisions (fast but opaque to customer accounting).
3) Disable TSO/GSO passthrough on the edge instance (reduces throughput but prevents large L4 segments on the wire).

I recommend MSS clamp + port pool widen as the least customer-impacting first step. Karthik and Marissa, can you validate command set and runbook?

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com

On Wed, Oct 14, 2026 at 09:05 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Escalating — StrataCorp is seeing TCP resets + large payloads failing after our private cutover.

I've pulled the edge device config diff and BGP adjacencies — attaching patch "bgp-config-diff.patch" and a short diff of the NAT table. Key observations:
- We introduced a SNAT translation rewrite to consolidate customer flows behind a smaller ephemeral pool (to reduce costly conntrack state). That change included a new L4 hashing permutation which can alias two tuples into same 16-bit port under heavy churn.
- Edge kernel offload flags were toggled (GSO enabled) to improve throughput; MSS clamp was not applied per-customer.

Plan to move forward (with times):
- 10:45 PDT apply MSS clamp to 1400 on egress for StrataCorp prefix (quick test window).
- 11:00 PDT monitor client uploads and conntrack table for aliasing. If uploads still fail, widen SNAT port pool and disable GSO passthrough.
- If both fail, rollback NAT rewrite to previous allocation scheme (estimated 15m).

Alex: can you confirm a low-traffic test bucket we can use at 11:00? We'll coordinate live with you and provide packet captures.

Karthik
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

—Alex
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: alex.ramos@stratacorp.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation summary and next steps

Alex / team — summary of what we executed and results: 
- 2026-10-14 10:45 PDT: Applied MSS clamp 1400 on egress for StrataCorp prefix. Immediate retest with "strata-test-11" upload: success (200MB completed).
- Observed reduction in retransmits and no 413s during the test window. Server-side pcaps show MTU fragmentation was being triggered when large segments were passed without clamp + GSO.
- 2026-10-14 11:20 PDT: Widened SNAT port pool as a precaution. No collisions observed thereafter.
- 2026-10-14 11:40 PDT: Disabled GSO passthrough on the edge instance for the StrataCorp route. Performance regression minimal on test bucket (<8% throughput drop), but stability restored for large uploads.

Action items: 
- Karthik: file a follow-up RFC to make per-customer MSS clamp part of rollout playbook for on-prem cutovers. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NET-4382
- Vivek: add a guard in the orchestration to not toggle offload flags without automatic per-prefix MSS clamp.
- Olga / Marissa: schedule a 1-hour postmortem with StrataCorp next week to review cutover runbook changes (I'll propose times).

Attaching final traces and a diff of NAT allocation for the incident artifacts. Closing the urgent escalation; we'll remain available for extended validation.

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

—Olga Petrov
Sr. Network Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
